args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service was failing health checks (healthy=false, error rate 18%) in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before the production deploy. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 as a SEV2.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The service was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. A follow-up check shows the service as healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and it paged the on-call engineer. It also notes that the test build of v2.3.1 was already unhealthy in staging before it went to production. The incident asks for the root cause in v2.3.1 to be found before anyone redeploys it.
